comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C82-C89 regarding sybody binding patterns in heteromeric assemblies. Both evaluations support the use of subunit-specific markers to distinguish CALHM2 and CALHM4 positions, with reviewers praising the methodological approach and cautious interpretation of mixed subunit positions.

Strong alignment on electrophysiology claims C51-C55. OpenEval supports the functional differences between CALHM1/3 and CALHM2/4 systems. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data validity but note as a limitation that no currents were observed for CALHM2/4 heteromers (C136), highlighting the lack of functional characterization.

Strong agreement on structural incompatibility claims C120-C123 explaining heteromer specificity. Both evaluations support the structural basis for why certain CALHM paralogs cannot form heteromers. OpenEval notes these are structural predictions rather than direct measurements, while peer reviewers accept the interpretation as part of comprehensive analysis.

Agreement on claims C125, C129, C130 regarding broad stoichiometry distribution and homomer preference. Both evaluations support these findings, though peer reviewers note the limitation that observations are from overexpressed systems. The comparison to LRRC8 assemblies is accepted by both.

Agreement on claims C45-C46 regarding CALHM2/4 complex formation from pulldown assays. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval additionally addresses C119 on heteromer specificity, which peer reviewers discuss separately in R11.

Alignment on subunit segregation claims C79-C81. OpenEval supports findings based on cryo-EM classification and sybody markers. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the segregation pattern, noting the distinct arrangement where orthologs interact but preferentially segregate. OpenEval R8 covers broader heteromer assembly claims (C77-C81) while peer R2 focuses on segregation with additional stoichiometry claims.

Strong agreement on conformational claims C90-C93, C131-C132. Both evaluations support that CALHM4 maintains its homomeric conformation while CALHM2 is influenced by proximity to CALHM4. OpenEval provides detailed structural analysis while peer reviewers affirm the clear results supporting these conclusions.

Partial overlap on abstract claims. OpenEval R19 addresses stoichiometry distribution (C6, C47) and subunit segregation (C7, C48) plus conformational features (C49, C50). Peer R2 focuses on segregation claims C47-C48 and related detailed claims C79-C81, providing explicit reviewer affirmation of the segregation pattern.

Agreement on sybody characterization claims C56-C58. Both evaluations support the nanobody development and specificity. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary techniques (SEC, SPR, cryo-EM), while peer reviewers praise the innovative use of synthetic nanobodies as fiducial markers. Peer R4 also covers C64-C65 on CALHM2 sybody binding.

Agreement on CALHM4 homomeric structure claims C59-C62. Both evaluations support the 3.7Å cryo-EM structure and architectural features. Peer R5 covers broader structural findings including CALHM2 undecamer (C64-C67) and conformational differences (C68-C69, C71-C72), while OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on CALHM4 structure.

Partial alignment on CALHM2 characterization. OpenEval R5 addresses biochemical and structural evidence for CALHM2 undecamer (C64-C67) with sybody binding. Peer R4 covers sybody methodology (C56-C58, C64-C65) with emphasis on the innovative fiducial marker approach for distinguishing subunits.

Agreement on CALHM2 structural features C68-C72. Both evaluations support the conformational differences from CALHM4 observed in the 3.1Å structure. Peer R5 provides broader affirmation of detailed structural insights, while OpenEval focuses on specific conformational analysis and comparison to rubidium red-bound structure.

Agreement on pore density observations C98-C99. Both evaluations support the correlation between subunit conformation and pore density features. OpenEval notes consistency with homomeric structures, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the comprehensive conformational analysis supporting overall conclusions.

Agreement on buried surface area analysis C100-C104. Both evaluations support the structural measurements and their correlation with interaction strength. Peer R7 covers broader interface analysis (C105-C114) including C-terminal organization differences, while OpenEval R12 focuses on buried surface calculations and energetic inferences.

Strong agreement on detailed interface analysis C105-C112. Both evaluations support the structural characterization of subunit interfaces and C-terminal organization differences between CALHM2 and CALHM4. Peer R7 also includes heteromer formation explanation (C113-C114), affirming the comprehensive structural analysis.

Agreement on heteromer formation explanation C113-C114. Both evaluations support the synthesis of structural complementarity (allowing heteromer formation) with energetic preference (explaining homomer predominance). This represents logical integration of structural and biochemical observations.

Alignment on functional uncertainty. OpenEval R18 addresses lack of heteromer activity (C136) and speculative explanations (C137-C138), noting primary claim is supported but mechanisms uncertain. Peer R10 evaluates uncertainty about physiological function (C118, C137-C138), acknowledging limitations of overexpression system and unknown functional effects.

Partial agreement on conformational independence claims C131-C132. OpenEval R17 addresses subunit conformational autonomy with coupling (C131-C134) based on structural data. Peer R3 covers broader conformational findings (C49-C50, C90-C93, C131-C132), affirming CALHM4 maintains conformation while CALHM2 is influenced by proximity.

OpenEval R7 addresses sybody binding interface details (C73-C76) including CT+1 involvement and non-overlapping binding. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though the overall sybody methodology is praised in peer R4.

Partial overlap on abstract conformational claims. OpenEval R19 validates abstract claims C49-C50 about maintained structural features with conformational influence, supported by detailed results. Peer R3 addresses these same claims plus detailed conformational analysis (C90-C93, C131-C132), affirming the findings.
